title: Contract tests and observability for fidelity-aware SLOs (model-fallback accuracy guards)
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: Redwood supports automated model fallbacks (e.g., quantized or smaller variants) to maintain availability and reduce cost when primary capacity is constrained. Current rollout gates focus on latency/availability, but we lack a reproducible, contractual test and monitoring surface for semantic fidelity degradations introduced by fallback variants. This ticket defines the PRD-level acceptance criteria, test harnesses, metrics, and rollout gates required to declare a fidelity-aware SLO that can be used in host-customer contracts and automated rollout policies.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Define a canonical golden request set (GRS) that covers representative request classes (chat-turn, single-turn prompt, embedding similarity, reranking) with at least 2k examples per class and per region.

A2: Specify per-class fidelity metrics and thresholds: e.g., semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) >= 0.92 top-1 for retrieval prompts, BLEU/ROUGE or chrF bounds for structured generation tasks, and top-k ranked-answer overlap >= 0.88 for reranking.

A3: Offline regression test: any model variant proposed as a fallback must pass a daily synthetic regression run against the GRS with measured degradation <= 1.5% absolute relative to baseline (hosted-production primary model) for all per-class metrics.

A4: Online canary acceptance: canary rollout (1% traffic, min 48h, min 2,000 requests per class) must show no regression > 2.0% on any fidelity metric and p95 latency within the contracted latency band for that class.

A5: Observability: fidelity metrics (GRS aggregate and rolling 1h window) must be ingested into Console dashboards and have alerting thresholds that map fidelity regressions to error-budget consumption (see test_plan).
A6: Contract mapping: translate fidelity metric breaches to customer-visible SLA terms (e.g., degraded-cosine event = minor SLA incident, repeated or >5% customers affected = P1 escalation).
test_plan: T1: Build GRS and store as versioned artifact (Confluence link + S3 path). Each entry tagged with request-class, region, and expected label/embedding baseline.
T2: Offline CI: integrate grafted evaluation harness (eval infra ENG-PR repo) to run nightly regressions and produce per-variant diffs and heatmaps.
T3: Shadow canary: run fallback variant in shadow mode on 5% traffic to gather live distribution metrics for 72h before active canary.
T4: A/B canary: route 1% production traffic, collect fidelity metrics and user-visible error logs. Minimum sample sizes per class required (2k requests/class).

T5: Automated rollback triggers: if any fidelity metric regression exceeds the gate (2.0% absolute) OR if customer errors or complaint rate increases by >30% over baseline, execute immediate rollback.
T6: Post-deploy continuous evaluation: daily drift report vs baseline and weekly summary emailed to PM/Eng/Research owners.
metrics_to_monitor: M1: Per-class semantic similarity (embedding cosine) distributions and top-1/top-5 overlap vs baseline
M2: Generation fidelity proxies (BLEU/ROUGE/chrF) for templated tasks
M3: Reranking top-k overlap and MRR delta
M4: Latency P50/P95/P99 per-class (TTFB for streaming classes)
M5: Availability/error-rate for fallback variant (5xx, model-runtime-errors)
M6: Customer-facing error/complaint rate and Support tickets attributed to degradation
M7: Canary traffic volume and sample sizes per-request-class
rollout_gates: G1: Shadow pass — fallback variant must have 0 functional errors during 72h shadowing on 5% traffic and match baseline invocation footprints (avg tokens, avg KV cache hits) within +/-10%.
G2: Offline regression gate — nightly GRS run must report <=1.5% absolute degradation across all metrics for three consecutive nights before scheduling canary.
G3: Canary gate — 1% traffic, min 48h, min 2k requests/class, fidelity regression <=2.0% absolute, no P95 latency violation > SLA band, and no spike in customer errors (>30% over baseline).
G4: Gradual ramp — on successful canary, ramp traffic to 10% for 24h, to 25% for 24h, with continuous monitoring; abort on any metric breach and rollback immediately.
G5: Emergency rollback — any single-region fidelity regression >3.5% or multiregion degradation affecting >5% of customers triggers automated rollback and page to SRE/PM/Research.
G6: Post-rollout probation — after reaching 100% traffic, continue fidelity sampling for 14 days and require weekly SLO reports for 8 weeks before marking as GA for contractual mapping.
risks: R1: GRS coverage may not represent future user prompts — risk of blind spots; mitigate by iterative expansion and lightweight in-prod prompt-sampling labeling.
R2: Embedding drift between model versions might require rebaseline of customer indices — ensure reindexing playbooks and customer communications documented.
R3: Observability gaps (missing per-class tagging) could make online checks unreliable — dependency on ENG instrumentation tasks.
R4: Computational cost of daily GRS runs on large models — may require scheduling and quota planning with infra/finance.
notes: Note 1: This ticket defines acceptance at the product/contract level; engineering tickets should break down the evaluation harness, metric ingestion, and automation for rollback gates.
Note 2: Where possible, use existing eval infra and embedding pipeline (see related_docs) to avoid duplicate work; create small PR for canonical GRS format spec.
Note 3: Consider adding a ‘fidelity tax’ mapping in billing UI to reflect customers that opt into lower-cost fallback variants with explicit consent.
